product: Two approved therapies: BRINSUPRI (brensocatib), an oral once-daily DPP1 inhibitor for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis approved in the US, EU, UK and Japan, and ARIKAYCE, inhaled amikacin liposome for MAC lung disease. Pipeline includes TPIP, INS1148, INS1033, INS1201 and INS1202.
demand: Strong for BRINSUPRI: the US launch generated 309.2M dollars in Q2 2026, up 49 percent quarter on quarter, with management citing significant enthusiasm and demand from patients and physicians. ARIKAYCE demand is mature in the US, plus 2 percent, but growing internationally at plus 19 percent. The NCFB population was previously untreated.
pricing_power: Moderate to strong on BRINSUPRI as the only approved NCFB therapy in the US, EU, UK and Japan. Realised net price is cut by Medicaid, Medicare Part D and managed-care rebates, chargebacks and co-payment assistance; no price increases were disclosed. Evolving US policies may affect timing of future international launches.
competition: The 10-Q cites a highly competitive and changing environment, and warns competitors may obtain orphan drug exclusivity for essentially equivalent products. BRINSUPRI has no approved NCFB competitor today; ARIKAYCE competes with other NTM treatment regimens; TPIP would compete with existing PAH and ILD prostanoids (aggregator context).
team: Chair and CEO Will Lewis; CFO Sara Bonstein; Chief Medical Officer Martina Flammer; Chief Product Strategy Officer Gene Sullivan. Samuele Butera was appointed Senior Vice President and General Manager Global Respiratory on 2026-06-23, with Makoto Nakamura leading Japan. Around 1,664 employees; insiders hold 0.62 percent.
market_strategy: Ramp BRINSUPRI in the US and prepare Japan launch, expand ARIKAYCE to earlier-line MAC in the US and Japan, run TPIP Phase 3 in PAH, PH-ILD, PPF and IPF, submit one to two INDs per year, keep preclinical research under 20 percent of spend, and use partners such as PARI and AstraZeneca with AI across operations.
bull: BRINSUPRI Q2 2026 revenue $309.2M, up 49% q/q, only approved NCFB therapy in US/EU/UK/Japan; 2026 guidance raised to $1.25-1.40B; FDA Priority Review PDUFA 2027-01-28 for ARIKAYCE earlier-line MAC.
bear: Net loss $13.2M, TTM loss $875M, negative FCF ~$808M; ARIKAYCE US +2%; Roth cut 212->198 (2026-09-15), JPM cut to 175 (2026-08-10); customer concentration A 38%, B 22%; shares below 200-day average.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-29 show BRINSUPRI revenue below the pace needed for the $1.25-1.40B 2026 guidance, forcing a guidance cut.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 results 2026-08-06: total revenue 425.5M dollars, BRINSUPRI 309.2M, net loss 13.2M; 2026 BRINSUPRI guidance raised to 1.25-1.40B dollars and peak estimates raised above 14B dollars. Japan MHLW approved BRINSUPRI 2026-08-24. FDA accepted the ARIKAYCE sNDA with Priority Review, PDUFA 2027-01-28, disclosed 2026-09-21.
web_not_known_yesterday: No company disclosure dated 2026-09-25 was found. Freshest item: Goldman Sachs initiated coverage at Buy with a 188 dollar price target on 2026-09-24. Shares closed 121.55, up 2.71 percent.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is volume and demand led, not price. BRINSUPRI US launch produced 309.2M dollars in Q2 2026, up 49 percent quarter on quarter. ARIKAYCE US grew only 2 percent on a refractory-only label, while international rose 19 percent. The guidance raise reflects demand; no price increases disclosed.
web_suppliers: Insmed relies on third-party manufacturers and suppliers; the 10-Q warns supply failure could materially impact results. ARIKAYCE is delivered only through PARI Pharma Lamira nebulizer, a licensed relationship, and AstraZeneca AB is also a licensor. Manufacturing-facility capacity leases imply reserved CDMO capacity; no specific constraint disclosed.
web_customers: Highly concentrated. Six months to 2026-06-30 gross product revenue: Customer A 38 percent, Customer B 22 percent, Customer C 18 percent, Customer D 14 percent (10-Q). US customers are specialty pharmacies and a specialty distributor; federal public-health buyers via the Federal Supply Schedule generate chargebacks.
web_who_loses: Filings describe a highly competitive and changing environment. BRINSUPRI is the only approved NCFB therapy in the US, EU, UK and Japan, so symptom-management care and older NTM, PAH and ILD regimens lose share. Specific rival names are not in the filings read; named PAH prostanoid comparators are aggregator context only.
web_contradicting_evidence: US ARIKAYCE grew only 2 percent; net loss still 13.2M dollars and TTM loss 875M with negative free cash flow. Weiss Ratings reiterated Sell D- on 2026-07-17; JPMorgan cut its target to 175 on 2026-08-10; Roth MKM cut 212 to 198 on 2026-09-15; Guggenheim cut on 2026-08-07. Shares are down 16.39 percent over 52 weeks, below the 135.51 200-day average, and funds exited on disappointing uptake (2026-09-10, aggregator).
web_if_management_right: ARIKAYCE wins full earlier-line MAC approval (PDUFA 2027-01-28), BRINSUPRI ramps in the US and launches in Japan, and TPIP succeeds across four Phase 3 indications. Combined peak sales exceed 14B dollars, 2026 revenue approaches 1.8B dollars, losses narrow toward profitability, and Q3 results (estimated 2026-10-29) bring further guidance raises.
web_if_management_wrong: Guidance breaks first: BRINSUPRI US uptake or net price misses the 1.25-1.40B dollar range and forces a cut. Negative free cash flow of about 808M dollars over twelve months against roughly 1.2B dollars of cash pushes another equity raise, with share count already up 18.73 percent year on year. A TPIP Phase 3 or PDUFA setback compounds the fall.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: PARI Pharma via the Lamira nebulizer licence and device supply, Insmed's third-party manufacturers and amikacin API suppliers, the four concentrated specialty pharmacy and distributor customers, licensor AstraZeneca AB, contract research organisations running the TPIP Phase 3 programme, and partners in the EMBARC bronchiectasis collaboration announced June 2026.
